Students can explore these themes by:

Analyzing real-world video commercials that use these techniques.
Creating their own short-form commercials incorporating Modernist framing, meme aesthetics, or collage-style editing.
Experimenting with remixing existing footage to create new narratives using found footage, glitch effects, or surreal animations.

description.describe_eh:
In this course, students learn to apply interactive design thinking to do marketing planning and utilize interactive technology to enhance public participation.
To achieve this, students are expected to understand following interrelated knowledge and skill sets: (1) essential concepts of participatory marketing; (2) recent trends in participatory marketing; (3) interactive technology and design methods; (4) skills to apply interactive design in emerging social media to increase consumer participation.

gradeRuleDescribe.course_pol:
課堂上的行為始終應要及時、要專業、要做好準備、要有禮貌。同學、教師或其他講師間，應保有彼此尊嚴和相互尊重，才能進行有效的學習。為了確保有利於學習環境，冀望每個人都能做到以下幾點，彼此遵守課堂行為規則，習慣禮貌的文化。

• 學生應準時出席上課。如果您的上課時間，無法按時到課，請不要選課。 除非您生病或有緊急情況，否則應在上課前，要準時到達教室，並坐在位子上。如果您有某種原因必須提早下課，請提前告知我。
• 所有學生在課堂上都應尊重每個人，並且在任何時候都應以合理、負責和禮貌的態度行事。
• 上課時請勿講話、閱讀、睡覺或做其他非本課程相關作業，除分組進行討論外，否則應盡量減少邊際對話。
• 當同學簡報或提問時，您應該專心地聆聽。當您簡報時，您應該面對自己的小組或全班同學大聲說話，讓同學能聽清楚。
• 允許使用筆記型電腦或平板等載具，進行課堂記筆記，否則應將其收起。
• 要確保在上課時，關閉手機、PDA等移動設備，並收起及保持靜音。
• 不得戴耳機上課。
• 穿著整潔，不要暴露。
• 冀望以最高標準、互相尊重的專業對話模式，以多樣化和包容性，講述課程規則內容。
• 教師得以引導學生方式，學習過程中學生要做的事，應有的責任。
• 希望同學在課堂上不要使用影印及盜版教材。上課期間在課堂上（不得吃食），不得趴睡。若有需要短暫休息或進食，可以暫時離開教室，相關事宜若已完成或排除，應盡快返回課堂上課。
gradeRuleDescribe.course_pol_en:
### **Course Policies**  

#### **1. Attendance and Participation**  
- Students are expected to **attend all classes and actively participate** in discussions, workshops, and presentations.  
- More than **three unexcused absences** may result in a **grade deduction**.  
- If a student must miss class due to illness or emergency, they should notify the instructor in advance and provide appropriate documentation if necessary.  

#### **2. Late Submission Policy**  
- Assignments and projects are **due on the specified deadline**. Late submissions will be penalized as follows:  
  - **1-3 days late**: 10% deduction per day.  
  - **More than 3 days late**: Not accepted unless prior approval is granted.  
- Extensions may be granted under **exceptional circumstances** with prior communication.  

#### **3. Classroom Etiquette and Professionalism**  
- Respectful discussion and professional conduct are expected at all times.  
- Disruptive behavior (e.g., excessive phone use, side conversations) may lead to **participation grade deductions**.  
- Students should **respect intellectual property** and avoid unauthorized use of copyrighted materials in presentations and projects.  

#### **4. Group Work and Collaboration**  
- For group assignments, all team members must contribute equally.  
- **Freeloading or non-participation** may result in **individual grade adjustments**.  
- If conflicts arise within a group, they should be resolved professionally, and if necessary, the instructor should be informed.  

#### **5. Use of Technology in Class**  
- Laptops and tablets may be used **for note-taking and research only**.  
- **No unauthorized recording** of lectures or class discussions.  
- Phones should be on silent and used only for class-related purposes.  

#### **6. Academic Integrity**  
- Plagiarism, unauthorized AI-generated content, or cheating will **not be tolerated**.  
- Violations may result in penalties ranging from **grade deductions to course failure**, in accordance with university policies.  

#### **7. Communication and Office Hours**  
- Course announcements will be made via the **university platform or email**. Students are responsible for checking updates regularly.  
- Office hours will be available for additional guidance. Students are encouraged to schedule appointments in advance.  

#### **8. Assessment and Grading**  
- Grades will be based on:  
  - Class Participation & Attendance (20%)  
  - Assignments & Case Studies (30%)  
  - Group Project & Presentation (30%)  
  - Final Exam or Final Report (20%)  
- Detailed rubrics will be provided for all major assignments.

gradeRuleDescribe.ais_meno_en:
Academic Integrity and Expectations
Students are expected to uphold the highest standards of academic integrity in all aspects of this course, including learning assessments, classroom interactions, and final performance evaluations. Any form of dishonesty, plagiarism, or unethical behavior will be subject to disciplinary action in accordance with university policies.
1. Learning Assessments (Assignments, Projects, and Exams)
  • Original Work: All submitted work must be the student’s own. Proper citation of sources is required when referencing external ideas, images, or media.
  • Plagiarism & AI Use: Directly copying from sources, unauthorized AI-generated content without proper attribution, or excessive reliance on AI tools for assignments is considered plagiarism.
  • Collaboration & Unauthorized Assistance: While group work is encouraged in designated projects, individual assessments must be completed independently unless explicitly stated otherwise.
Possible Disciplinary Actions:
  • First offense: Warning and revision of the assignment.
  • Second offense: Grade reduction or failure for the assessment.
  • Repeated offenses: Possible course failure and referral to the academic integrity office.
2. Interactions in Class
  • Respect & Professionalism: Students must engage respectfully with peers and instructors, fostering a constructive learning environment.
  • Ethical Use of Media: Any visual, film, or marketing content used in class discussions should respect copyright and ethical standards.
  • Constructive Criticism: Feedback on peer work should be professional and focused on academic improvement.
Possible Disciplinary Actions:
  • Disruptive behavior: Verbal warning or deduction in participation grades.
  • Harassment, discrimination, or offensive behavior: Immediate disciplinary review, potential removal from class discussions.
3. End-of-Course Performance & Final Project
  • Honest Representation of Work: Students must accurately represent their efforts in final projects, including creative work, research, and practical applications.
  • No Fabrication of Data: If research or case studies are involved, falsifying data or results is strictly prohibited.
  • Professional Presentation: Final presentations should reflect a high level of effort, academic rigor, and ethical considerations.
Possible Disciplinary Actions:
  • Failure to meet integrity standards in the final project may result in point deductions or a requirement to redo portions of the work.
  • Severe violations (e.g., fraudulent data, major plagiarism) may result in failure of the course.
Conclusion
Academic integrity is essential for both personal growth and professional development. Students are encouraged to ask questions when unsure about proper citation, collaboration policies, or ethical considerations. Any violations will be handled according to university regulations, with fairness and due process.

policy.course_pol_en:
### **Course Policies**  

#### **1. Attendance and Participation**  
- Students are expected to **attend all classes and actively participate** in discussions, workshops, and presentations.  
- More than **three unexcused absences** may result in a **grade deduction**.  
- If a student must miss class due to illness or emergency, they should notify the instructor in advance and provide appropriate documentation if necessary.  

#### **2. Late Submission Policy**  
- Assignments and projects are **due on the specified deadline**. Late submissions will be penalized as follows:  
  - **1-3 days late**: 10% deduction per day.  
  - **More than 3 days late**: Not accepted unless prior approval is granted.  
- Extensions may be granted under **exceptional circumstances** with prior communication.  

#### **3. Classroom Etiquette and Professionalism**  
- Respectful discussion and professional conduct are expected at all times.  
- Disruptive behavior (e.g., excessive phone use, side conversations) may lead to **participation grade deductions**.  
- Students should **respect intellectual property** and avoid unauthorized use of copyrighted materials in presentations and projects.  

#### **4. Group Work and Collaboration**  
- For group assignments, all team members must contribute equally.  
- **Freeloading or non-participation** may result in **individual grade adjustments**.  
- If conflicts arise within a group, they should be resolved professionally, and if necessary, the instructor should be informed.  

#### **5. Use of Technology in Class**  
- Laptops and tablets may be used **for note-taking and research only**.  
- **No unauthorized recording** of lectures or class discussions.  
- Phones should be on silent and used only for class-related purposes.  

#### **6. Academic Integrity**  
- Plagiarism, unauthorized AI-generated content, or cheating will **not be tolerated**.  
- Violations may result in penalties ranging from **grade deductions to course failure**, in accordance with university policies.  

#### **7. Communication and Office Hours**  
- Course announcements will be made via the **university platform or email**. Students are responsible for checking updates regularly.  
- Office hours will be available for additional guidance. Students are encouraged to schedule appointments in advance.  

#### **8. Assessment and Grading**  
- Grades will be based on:  
  - Class Participation & Attendance (20%)  
  - Assignments & Case Studies (30%)  
  - Group Project & Presentation (30%)  
  - Final Exam or Final Report (20%)  
- Detailed rubrics will be provided for all major assignments.

policy.ais_meno_en:
Academic Integrity and Expectations
Students are expected to uphold the highest standards of academic integrity in all aspects of this course, including learning assessments, classroom interactions, and final performance evaluations. Any form of dishonesty, plagiarism, or unethical behavior will be subject to disciplinary action in accordance with university policies.
1. Learning Assessments (Assignments, Projects, and Exams)
  • Original Work: All submitted work must be the student’s own. Proper citation of sources is required when referencing external ideas, images, or media.
  • Plagiarism & AI Use: Directly copying from sources, unauthorized AI-generated content without proper attribution, or excessive reliance on AI tools for assignments is considered plagiarism.
  • Collaboration & Unauthorized Assistance: While group work is encouraged in designated projects, individual assessments must be completed independently unless explicitly stated otherwise.
Possible Disciplinary Actions:
  • First offense: Warning and revision of the assignment.
  • Second offense: Grade reduction or failure for the assessment.
  • Repeated offenses: Possible course failure and referral to the academic integrity office.
2. Interactions in Class
  • Respect & Professionalism: Students must engage respectfully with peers and instructors, fostering a constructive learning environment.
  • Ethical Use of Media: Any visual, film, or marketing content used in class discussions should respect copyright and ethical standards.
  • Constructive Criticism: Feedback on peer work should be professional and focused on academic improvement.
Possible Disciplinary Actions:
  • Disruptive behavior: Verbal warning or deduction in participation grades.
  • Harassment, discrimination, or offensive behavior: Immediate disciplinary review, potential removal from class discussions.
3. End-of-Course Performance & Final Project
  • Honest Representation of Work: Students must accurately represent their efforts in final projects, including creative work, research, and practical applications.
  • No Fabrication of Data: If research or case studies are involved, falsifying data or results is strictly prohibited.
  • Professional Presentation: Final presentations should reflect a high level of effort, academic rigor, and ethical considerations.
Possible Disciplinary Actions:
  • Failure to meet integrity standards in the final project may result in point deductions or a requirement to redo portions of the work.
  • Severe violations (e.g., fraudulent data, major plagiarism) may result in failure of the course.
Conclusion
Academic integrity is essential for both personal growth and professional development. Students are encouraged to ask questions when unsure about proper citation, collaboration policies, or ethical considerations. Any violations will be handled according to university regulations, with fairness and due process.
